data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word catarina, meaning pure or innocent. In the Christian context, it can be interpreted as a reminder to strive for a pure and innocent heart. The name Catrina carries the meaning “Pure, innocent” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Catrina usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, innocent and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of purity and innocence in the spiritual journey.
data.etymology: Catrina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Pure, innocent.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Catrina total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.
data.cultural_impact: The name Catrina, particularly in Mexico, has cultural significance as it is associated with the Day of the Dead (Día de los Muertos). The legend of La Catrina, a female skull decoration, represents the memento mori concept – a reminder of the fleeting nature of life and the inevitability of death. It is celebrated through festivities, art, and music, and the name Catrina is often used in reference to the iconic figure.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Catrina, from its roots as a Latin word meaning pure or innocent, carries a deep spiritual significance. It is a call to remember our true nature and identity, which is pure and innocent, despite our human tendencies towards sin and impurity. In Christian beliefs, this purity is referred to as sanctification, which involves being set apart for God and growing closer to Him through the process of transformation. Practicing the virtues of faith, hope, and charity while striving for a pure heart allows us to connect with God, attain inner peace, and ultimately fulfil our God-given potential.
